newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil re-election vote suffers another delay.
newsitem.headline: Brazil re-election vote suffers another delay.

text.p: Voting by Brazil's Congress on a bill allowing President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run again in 1998 was put back for a second time on Tuesday as the government struggled to bring a key ally back into the fold.
"Technically we could vote at any time, tomorrow even, but we expect it will take place on Tuesday (next week)," said Jose Anibal, a government whip in the Chamber of Deputies.

Cardoso, seeking to become Brazil's first re-elected president, called a special session of Congress to run through the January recess in the hope of getting lower house approval for a constitutional amendment allowing re-election.

But opposition within the Brazilian Democratic Movement Party (PMDB), the biggest in Congress and normally part of Cardoso's fragile, multi-party alliance, forced the government to postpone a vote on the bill last week and again this week.
"We're going to sit down with the PMDB and try to get them to rejoin the government's alliance in Congress," said a govenment source who asked not to be identified.

Senior figures within the PMDB have told party deputies not to vote until Feb. 15 to make sure the government does not back rival candidates in upcoming elections to preside over the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate.
"(The PMDB) is taking advantage of the overlapping of re-election and the congressional elections to strengthen their grip on power," said Paulo Kramer, a politics professor at Brasilia University.

The government wants to push re-election through the Chamber of Deputies quickly to resume progress on other reforms to streamline the state that are considered crucial to the long-term success of its economic programme.
